answer: He opened forty accounts in one night, sure fresh names were a haven from reputation. Each needed a continuity chain: every epoch it publishes work hashing to its own last output, and peers attest only work on a chain they have seen. Faking forty histories meant forty chains at once, and one paragraph reused across two sent a ripple through the onyx registry and voided both. By epoch three, odds compounded: eight checks at 70% each left every fake under 6%. He kept two alive; thirty-eight died quietly. A real newcomer starts at zero too, earning it epoch by epoch.
